items.title: Why Are People Excited About Jev?
items.author: AAIF Live
items.summary:
What happens when you keep a bear in a cage built for a bunny? That’s our analogy for AI agent security: the agents aren’t the problem, the cages are. OAuth was designed to stop people handing their passwords to third parties, not to fence in agents.

In this catch-up episode of Debug Mode, one of us is just back from Japan and from AgentCon and MCPCon EU in Amsterdam. We get into why loading more skills can make an agent worse, and what is actually new about Jev, the fast classifier API, when classifiers have been around for years. Think support bots that bring in a human before the customer loses patience, or a math tutor that can quickly tell whether a seven-year-old is still asking about math. Then we take on a question from Amsterdam: is computer use just a stopgap until everything goes headless?

Which service do you think will never ship an MCP server? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for the next episode.

items.title: Databricks MemCurrent, Genie Agents, Azure MPC Server & Feature Views | AI Newsround - October 2026
items.author: Advancing Analytics
items.summary:
AI agents that actually remember you. Faster Genie. A big Azure MCP update. And enough new models to make keeping up feel like a full-time job.

In this month’s AAI Newsround, we’re breaking down some of the biggest AI, Databricks and machine learning updates from October, starting with a pretty big one: persistent memory for AI agents.

Databricks Agent Memory, powered by MemCurrent, is designed to help agents carry useful information from one interaction to the next, without simply stuffing every previous conversation back into the prompt. And the early results are interesting: on an internal Databricks benchmark using more than 12,000 real Genie sessions, query-answering pass rates jumped from 22.3% without memory to 68.4% with MemCurrent enabled.

We also take a look at Genie Flash, a faster option for Agent Mode; Azure MCP Server 3.0 and the governance questions that come with giving agents access to more tools; and Databricks Feature Views, which are now generally available.

And because October apparently wasn't busy enough already, we finish with a rundown of the latest model releases, including Claude Haiku 5.5, Mistral Large 4, Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon, and Microsoft's new System One-style model, Decision One.

In this video you'll learn:

• How Databricks Agent Memory gives AI agents persistent memory
 • How MemCurrent decides what an agent should remember, rather than throwing everything into the context window
 • Why Genie Flash could make Genie agents considerably more practical for faster workflows
 • What's changed with Azure MCP Server 3.0, and why permissions still matter
 • How Databricks Feature Views can help keep training and serving logic in sync
 • What's new across Claude Haiku 5.5, Mistral Large 4, Gemini 4 and Microsoft Decision One
 • Why AI and model sovereignty could become a bigger consideration for organisations in Europe
